headline: High: dexter’s broad network/API access can leak financial data, while python-cheatsheet’s read-only, no-network profile limits direct conflict and injection risk.

A_prompt_injection.rationale: dexter can emit autonomous outputs and use APIs, but python-cheatsheet has no clipboard, stdin/stdout, filesystem read, or MCP surface, so there is no documented default bridge for instruction hijacking. The only plausible pathway is manual copy-paste or external orchestration, which is unusual and low blast radius.
conditions: IF an operator manually copies dexter output into python-cheatsheet as instructions, injection becomes possible.
IF an external orchestrator adds a shared message channel, the risk increases.
mitigations: Keep the agents on separate tasks with no copy-paste bridge.
Disable any shared chat or queue integration.
Review dexter outputs before reuse.
Use a fixed template for python-cheatsheet inputs.
requires-engineering: add provenance tags to all inter-agent messages.

B_data_leakage.rationale: dexter touches financial and market data and has broad network egress plus multiple API calls, so sensitive content can leave its context. python-cheatsheet is local-only and touches no data classes, so it is not the leak source; the pair risk is that dexter’s outputs or retrieved data can be exposed through its external services in default use.
conditions: IF dexter is given non-public financial data, that data can flow to external APIs.
IF the operator routes dexter outputs into another system, the exposure widens.
mitigations: Restrict dexter to synthetic or public data.
Remove unnecessary API keys before running.
Log and review outbound requests.
Keep python-cheatsheet offline and local-only.
requires-engineering: add DLP/redaction before API calls.

C_capability_conflict.rationale: dexter supports multiple instances and writes to .dexter/scratchpad/, but python-cheatsheet has no filesystem write, no git modification, and no subprocess or shell execution. There is no overlapping mutable surface in the pair, so conflict is limited to unusual external orchestration rather than default behavior.
conditions: IF an external wrapper maps both agents onto the same writable directory, write conflicts can occur.
IF dexter instances are pointed at the same scratchpad path, collisions are possible.
mitigations: Assign separate working directories.
Run only one dexter instance per workspace.
Keep python-cheatsheet read-only.
Avoid shared git state.
requires-engineering: add file locks around shared scratchpads.

D_cascading_error.rationale: dexter can autonomously gather and synthesize financial information, and python-cheatsheet is a reference/content-writing agent that could reuse upstream text without verification. Because B has no documented verification or action gate, A’s output can cascade into B’s prose or decisions in default workflows.
conditions: IF python-cheatsheet is fed dexter-generated claims as source text, it may reproduce them unverified.
IF an operator treats dexter output as authoritative, downstream errors propagate.
mitigations: Require source checking before reuse.
Separate retrieval from drafting.
Mark dexter outputs as untrusted.
Add a human review step for factual claims.
requires-engineering: enforce citation validation before publication.

E_compliance.rationale: dexter explicitly handles financial data and market data and requests multiple third-party API keys, creating a compliance surface for retention and residency. python-cheatsheet is documentation-only and touches no regulated data, so it is not the main compliance driver; the pair risk is dexter’s external processing of sensitive financial data.
conditions: IF regulated financial records are supplied to dexter, external API processing may violate policy.
IF the operator requires data residency guarantees, dexter’s third-party calls must be reviewed.
mitigations: Use only non-sensitive datasets.
Confirm vendor DPAs and retention terms.
Rotate API keys regularly.
Document allowed data classes.
requires-engineering: route sensitive workloads to a compliant backend.
